title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Dipsacus keeps head-worm remedy carriers distinct from ear-worm recipients killed by leaf juice
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED_NO_MEANING_CLAIM. In the complete cached Lonitzer1551 Dipsacus entry, worms found in the plant head are enclosed/tied in a small container and hung at neck or arm as a cited quartan-fever remedy; later leaf juice kills worms of the ears. A joint exploratory content account must preserve the first creatures as carried remedy material and the second as affected recipients. Shared worm wording does not license co-reference, extraction of ear-worms as an ingredient, or a universal worm-killing property. Related head/pouch and leaf-juice branches are already retained; this combined role contrast is raw supply, not a reopened failed route or confirmed novelty.

design.mechanism: Two operation chains constrain the causal role of the named creatures: plant-head creatures in a carrier worn by a fever patient; ear creatures affected by leaf juice. Homonymous creature mention does not establish creature-token identity or shared remedy role.

design.prediction: Any later fixed hypothetical whole reading that claims this particular source argument must jointly distinguish head/source location, pouch carrier, neck-or-arm suspension, fever target, leaf-juice bearer, ear recipient location, and killing effect.
